subject: Data retention & PII handling - follow up from discovery
messages:
From: Alice Park <alice.park@finco-payments.com>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Date: 2026-02-10T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Data retention & PII handling - follow up from discovery

Camila / team,

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap from our side and a couple of clarifying questions so we can move toward a mutual action plan: 

- FinCo requirements (high level):
  - No persistent storage of raw PII (names, SSNs, cardholder data) from production traffic, effectively a 0-retention requirement for PII fields.
  - Data residency: US-only.
  - Auditability: we need access to retention logs/audit records for at least 90 days for compliance reviews (but these must not contain raw PII).
  - Debugging: we may need short-lived, redacted logs for troubleshooting (acceptable if redacted/hashed and TTL-limited).

Questions:
1) Can Redwood implement per-route retention policies so we can mark certain endpoints as 0-retention while allowing other telemetry?
2) What tooling do you provide to demonstrate proofs of deletion for PII (e.g., deletion job logs, retention TTLs, audit logs)?
3) Are there any platform telemetry or kernel-level traces that will always retain identifiable data?

If you can share a SOC2 snapshot and a proposed retention schedule (even draft) we can route to our InfoSec and Legal. Also, if you have a sample amendment (DocuSign-ready) for retention exceptions that would speed things up.

Thanks, happy to do a quick follow-up next week after you share docs.

Best,
Alice Park
Head of Privacy, FinCo Payments
alice.park@finco-payments.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Alice,

Appreciate the clear summary, great to align on scope. Recap + next steps from our side below: 

Recap of what we heard:
- Primary ask: 0-retention for raw PII in production traffic (session-only processing; no persistent logs containing PII).
- Secondary: US-only residency and ability to demonstrate retention/deletion for audit purposes.
- Debugging allowed with strict redaction + short TTLs.

What Redwood can do (high level):
- Per-route retention flags: we support per-endpoint retention policies you can toggle (e.g., 0d for PII endpoints, 7d aggregated telemetry for non-PII).
- Proofs of deletion: retention job logs and audit trail exports showing TTL enforcement and deletion timestamps; available via Console and as downloadable CSVs.
- Masking/Redaction: we offer tokenization and deterministic hashing for fields you mark as PII; hashed values can be kept for fraud/dedup but raw values are never persisted when route is configured for 0-retention.
- Data residency: hosted option with US-only region and dedicated routing for your traffic.

Attachments I'm sending now: SOC2-snapshot-2025.pdf (SOC2 summary & coverage) and a draft retention schedule (retention-schedule-proposal.pdf) that lays out a few options (0-retention, short logs, custom schedule). Also looping Legal/Policy (Marissa) and SE (Rafael) to comment.

Proposed next steps:
1) Marissa / Legal to review redline and confirm the exact fields FinCo considers PII.
2) Rafael to confirm implementation details and any engineering constraints.
3) Camila to schedule a follow-up (30-45m) to review redline + retention schedule, propose Wed 2/18 10:00 PT or Thu 2/19 9:00 PT.

Do any of those times work?

Thanks,
Camila Reyes

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Alice Park <alice.park@finco-payments.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com, camila_reyes@redwood.com
Date: 2026-02-12T10:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Data retention & PII handling - follow up from discovery

Hi all,

Thanks, technical confirmation and implementation notes below. TL;DR: the requested behaviors are feasible with standard Redwood configs, with a couple of clarifications and one operational note.

Feasibility / plan:
- Per-route retention: supported. We can tag routes as "pii: true" and apply a 0d TTL that prevents persistent storage of raw inputs/outputs. Runtime processes will process in-memory and purge caches/KV entries for those routes at TTL expiry.
- Proofs of deletion: we will provide retention job logs (timestamped) and an audit export showing deletion job runs and record counts. These exports will be generated from the Console and can be scheduled to S3 (US only) for your auditors.
- Debugging: we cannot retain raw PII in logs, but we can produce redacted logs where PII fields are replaced with deterministic hashes (configurable). We can keep those hashed records for 7 days by default; if FinCo needs shorter windows (e.g., 24h) we can configure that per-route.

Operational note:
- Platform telemetry: anonymized metrics (CPU, memory, token counts) are retained for 90 days and never contain raw PII. Low-level kernel traces occasionally include request IDs and short-lived identifiers; we can mask request IDs tied to PII routes and avoid storing them persistently. If FinCo requires elimination of any request-level identifiers, we recommend adding an explicit flag; that will limit our troubleshooting signal.

Deliverables I can provide:
- A retention-schedule-proposal.pdf (attached) with specific TTLs per data class.
- A sample Console export of a deletion job (CSV) showing job timestamps.
- A short runbook for FinCo's SREs describing how to configure per-route retention and redaction rules.

If this sounds good I'll update the redline with a short tech addendum that describes the TTLs and the proof-of-deletion artifacts.

Rafael Mendes
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.com

Attachments: retention-schedule-proposal.pdf
